title: Would SATURN Float in Your Bathtub? 🪐
description:
Drop Saturn in a bathtub and it would float. Cup for cup, Saturn is about 30% lighter than water: its average density is about 0.69 grams per cubic centimetre, water's is 1. That's because Saturn isn't rock: it's mostly hydrogen and helium, the two lightest things in the universe. Earth sinks, Jupiter sinks: of all the planets in our solar system, only Saturn floats. The catch: the bath would have to be wider than Saturn (about 120,000 km), and Saturn would probably fall apart in it: its dense core would sink, its gas would rise, and its icy rings would float. So yes, it leaves a ring. Did you guess sink or float?
